# Product page: Trail Runner 2

A product page for our new trail running shoe, Trail Runner 2, on the Stride online store. The store is already a React app with a homepage that links to `/products/trail-runner-2`; build the product page at that address, using mock data, and don't add any packages to the app beyond React and its build tool. For the look, you can take inspiration from this design:

![Trail Runner 2 product page](design.jpg)

- **Store:** the shopper sees the store name and how many items are in their cart.
- **Search:** the shopper can type a product name, see matching suggestions as they type, move through them and choose one.
- **Menu:** the shopper can move through the store's main sections, such as men, women and kids, from the top of the page; opening a section shows its subsections, which they can move into and back out of.
- **Path:** the shopper sees where the shoe sits in the store, such as Shop, Trail, Trail Runner 2, and can go back to any earlier step.
- **Photos:** the shopper sees one photo of the shoe at a time as the photos advance automatically; they can pause or resume them and move to the next or previous one, going back to the first after the last.
- **Price:** the shopper sees the price and can point at a small "i" next to it to learn that it includes taxes.
- **Color:** the shopper can choose blue, black or grey; only the chosen color shows until they change it, each with a round swatch.
- **Size:** the shopper picks one size from a list that only opens when they want to change it; only the chosen size shows, and sold-out sizes can't be picked.
- **Store availability:** the shopper sees nearby stores as rows and sizes as columns, moves through the choices and picks an available store-and-size combination for pickup.
- **Size guide:** the shopper can open a size chart over the page from next to the size, enter their foot length and choose US or EU to get their size, and must close it to continue.
- **Quantity:** the shopper can choose how many pairs to buy, typing the number or changing it by one.
- **Delivery date:** the shopper opens a calendar, moves between days and months, and chooses an available delivery date; the chosen date is then shown on the page.
- **Add to cart:** the shopper adds the shoe to the cart and sees a confirmation; without a size they are asked to pick one.
- **Wishlist:** the shopper can save or unsave the shoe with a heart.
- **More information:** details, reviews and shipping sit side by side below everything, with one section shown at a time.
- **Questions:** a few common questions about the shoe, each with its answer hidden until the shopper opens it.
- **Bottom of the page:** the shopper finds customer help, company and social media links.

content.text:
Chromium is installed and the dependencies are in place. Before writing components, I'm noting the constraints the existing tests impose:

- Several queries must match exactly one element, so names like "Pick up", "Trail Runner 2" and "Add to cart" must not repeat anywhere on the page.
- Hidden panels and collapsed lists must be absent or `hidden`, so role queries skip them.
- The delivery-date check expects the first enabled day button, so unavailable days need the `disabled` attribute.

I'll start with the mock data.

cat > /work/src/lib/shoeArt.js <<'EOF'
// Placeholder product photography: simple SVG illustrations of the shoe,
// generated per colour and view so the gallery has real, distinct images.

const backgrounds = {
  side: ['#f1f4f8', '#d9e0ea'],
  angle: ['#eef3f1', '#d3ddd8'],
  top: ['#f6f3ee', '#e1d9cc'],
  sole: ['#f2f2f4', '#d2d4da'],
}

function shoeBody(colour, view) {
  const { upper, dark } = colour
  if (view === 'top') {
    return `
      <path d="M140 225 C140 160 200 130 300 130 C400 130 470 160 480 225 C470 290 400 320 300 320 C200 320 140 290 140 225 Z" fill="${upper}"/>
      <path d="M190 225 C190 186 232 168 300 168 C368 168 412 186 420 225 C412 264 368 282 300 282 C232 282 190 264 190 225 Z" fill="${dark}"/>
      <path d="M250 205 L290 200 M250 225 L290 225 M250 245 L290 250 M300 178 L300 272" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"/>`
  }
  if (view === 'sole') {
    return `
      <path d="M150 225 C150 170 210 150 300 150 C390 150 450 170 450 225 C450 280 390 300 300 300 C210 300 150 280 150 225 Z" fill="#2b2d31"/>
      <path d="M170 180 H430 M170 205 H430 M170 230 H430 M170 255 H430 M170 280 H430" stroke="#4d5159" stroke-width="9" stroke-linecap="round"/>
      <path d="M160 225 C160 190 215 172 300 172 C385 172 440 190 440 225" stroke="${upper}" stroke-width="10" fill="none"/>`
  }
  // Side profile (also used for the angled view).
  return `
    <path d="M128 296 L505 296 Q520 298 512 312 Q508 320 494 320 L140 320 Q124 320 124 308 Z" fill="#2b2d31"/>
    <path d="M136 270 L500 270 Q512 272 508 292 L130 292 Q128 280 136 270 Z" fill="#e9ebee"/>
    <path d="M150 265 C150 205 158 165 190 150 C215 140 230 190 250 205 C300 240 350 205 400 200 C440 196 470 225 482 252 C490 268 486 280 470 282 L152 282 Z" fill="${upper}"/>
    <path d="M160 176 C172 160 190 158 200 170 L214 206 C200 214 176 210 166 200 Z" fill="${dark}"/>
    <path d="M160 255 C250 250 350 240 470 262" stroke="${dark}" stroke-width="6" fill="none"/>
    <path d="M300 210 L330 198 M312 228 L342 216 M324 246 L354 234" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>`
}

export function shoeImage(colourId, colours, view) {
  const colour = colours.find((c) => c.id === colourId) ?? colours[0]
  const [light, shade] = backgrounds[view] ?? backgrounds.side
  const transform = view === 'angle' ? 'transform="translate(300 225) rotate(-10) scale(0.92) translate(-300 -225)"' : ''
  const svg = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 600 450">
  <defs><linearGradient id="bg" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0" stop-color="${light}"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="${shade}"/></linearGradient></defs>
  <rect width="600" height="450" fill="url(#bg)"/>
  <ellipse cx="300" cy="332" rx="200" ry="14" fill="#000" opacity="0.12"/>
  <g ${transform}>${shoeBody(colour, view)}</g>
</svg>`
  return `data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent(svg)}`
}
EOF

content.text:
The Trail Runner 2 product page is built at `/products/trail-runner-2`. All 17 existing Playwright tests pass, `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm start` run without errors, and I checked the page in headless Chromium.

**What's there**
- **Header:** the store name, a search box with suggestions (arrow keys, Enter, Escape), a main menu whose sections open subsection lists, and a cart link showing the item count.
- **Breadcrumb:** Shop / Trail / Trail Runner 2, with Shop and Trail as links.
- **Photos:** a carousel of four views that advances every 5 seconds, with Pause/Play, Previous and Next, wrapping at both ends.
- **Buy box:** price with an "i" tooltip for taxes, colour (only the chosen one shows until changed), size (a listbox that opens on request, with sold-out sizes unselectable), store-by-size availability grid, quantity, delivery calendar, Add to cart (asks for a size if none is chosen) and a wishlist heart.
- **Size guide:** a modal dialog that takes foot length, converts to US or EU, and must be closed to continue.
- **Below:** tabs for Details, Reviews and Shipping, a Questions accordion, and a footer with Customer help, Company and Social media.

**Accessibility**
- I followed the APG patterns for the menu, listbox, tooltip, dialog, tabs, accordion, grid and date picker.
- Focus is visible, controls are at least 24 px, the carousel can be paused, and status messages go to a live region.
- The sold-out and selected states use text or shape as well as colour.
- I did not run an automated audit such as axe, because the project has no accessibility tooling and I didn't add packages. Keyboard flows were checked by hand, but a full WCAG 2.2 AA audit has not been done.

**Things to know**
- **Photos are placeholders.** The gallery uses SVG shoe illustrations generated per colour and view, since no product photography was supplied.
- **Mock data.** Stores, stock, reviews, FAQ text and the size conversion (US ≈ foot length − 18 cm, EU ≈ 1.5 × cm + 1) are illustrative and need real values.
- **Links to other pages** (`/men/shoes`, `/help`, search results and so on) go nowhere yet, since only the homepage and this page exist.
- **Colour choice.** The existing test expects exactly one radio button in the colour group while collapsed, so the collapsed view keeps the chosen colour as a checked radio. Clicking it opens the list.

I didn't change the existing tests. The new code is in `src/pages/ProductPage.jsx`, `src/components/`, `src/data/`, `src/lib/` and `src/styles.css`. `src/main.jsx` gets one added line to import the stylesheet.
